(1) Every readiness wait has a timeout. verify&#39;s startPreview loops against `deadline = Date.now() + 30_000`, each probe has `req.setTimeout(1000, () =&gt; req.destroy())`, and it throws &#39;not ready ... within 30s&#39; when the deadline passes. inspect&#39;s startPreview checks PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT_MS (30s), stops the preview and throws. The template copies hold identical code at the same line numbers. Judges A and B are borne out. If the start mode was 'present', the code presses 'p' to reach browse, then 'p' to go to present, then 'p' to return to browse, then a fourth 'p' to restore. If any toggle is swallowed, the verifier compares against the wrong mode or leaves the page in the wrong mode for the next ArrowRight step. The no-op 'p' case also can't be told apart from a real one. This can produce false failures or false passes.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/verify-helpers.mjs:33 parseRegistry uses a regex that only matches `slug: '...'` followed by `title:` inside the same braces with no nested `{}`. A registry entry that lists `title` before `slug`, or builds slugs from a variable or template with interpolation, yields an entry with `title: undefined`, or no entry at all. checkSampleRegistered then skips the title check when entry.title is undefined, so a wrong registered title passes silently. A reordered or computed registry also reports 'sample not registered' even though it works.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:183 The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers are registered with process.once and call cleanup().finally(process.exit(130)). cleanup() reads `preview` and `browser`, which are only assigned later. A signal arriving during `npm run build` (spawnSync, which blocks the event loop) or before startPreview resolves has nothing to clean up, which is fine. But a signal during startPreview leaves the already-spawned child unreferenced, because `preview` is assigned only after the await resolves. The vite preview process then survives as an orphan on the port.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/detect-scaffold.mjs:331 The `--apply` CLI sets the package name with slugify(basename(appDir)). An all-numeric or invalid npm name (for example a name starting with a digit or dot) is still written to package.json and package-lock.json unchecked. This can produce a package.json name that npm rejects.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/usePresentationNav.ts:109 The touchstart handler stores `start` from touches[0] without checking touches.length. A multi-touch gesture such as a pinch-zoom produces a touchend with changedTouches[0] for whichever finger lifted first. The delta is then measured against the other finger's start position, which can exceed the swipe threshold and trigger an unintended step change. There is also no touchcancel handler, so `start` goes stale after a cancelled gesture and the next touchend without a touchstart can pair with it.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/Root.tsx:29 Root computes the route from window.location.pathname once per render, but nothing listens for navigation. They don&#39;t re-implement the kit&#39;s mechanisms. Talk.tsx renders the kit&#39;s `Presentation` with `steps={STEPS}`, a title and `initialMode`. It has no navigation, stage, chrome or transition code of its own. `STEPS` in steps/index.ts is typed as the kit&#39;s `Step&lt;Beat&gt;[]`, and every step carries `Scene` and `groupKey`. Scene.tsx imports `Arrow`, `Box`, `Frame`, `SceneLayer`, `SymbolChip` and `SceneProps` from the kit&#39;s index. It builds every entity with those kit primitives and passes `id`, geometry and `emphasis`. Motion comes from `Box` and `Arrow` (`layout` plus `layoutId={id}`), and the kit&#39;s `Stage` supplies `LayoutGroup` and `AnimatePresence`. In reference mode, main() in scripts/verify.mjs reads the registry and calls checkSampleRegistered(registry, reference). This happens before startPreview() or any browser work. If the slug is missing, checkSampleRegistered throws VerifyError(&#39;sample-registration&#39;, &#39;reference sample &quot;…&quot; is not registered in src/presentations/index.ts&#39;). It also throws when the registry title is missing or different. slugsToVisit throws the same phase error when the registry is empty. The top-level catch prints formatFailure(err) as &#39;[verify] FAIL phase=sample-registration …&#39; and sets exitCode = 1. Missing or out-of-order step content is caught by explicit outline checks in walkPresentation. A wrong count reports &#39;step count is N, expected 9&#39;. compareStep reports &#39;title/caption/era is X, expected Y&#39; at the offending step. The e2e table runs these cases against a disposable copy and asserts code != 0, no PASS, and the expected FAIL phase and step. The cases are &#39;sample removed from the registry&#39;, &#39;registry has no entries&#39; (sample-registration), &#39;wrong step count (eight steps)&#39;, &#39;swapped titles (out of order)&#39; and &#39;swapped captions (out-of-order steps)&#39; (render, with step). This matches Judges A and C. Judge B&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. B relies on a steps array emptied while the sample stays registered and the build still passes. That is a constructed partial deletion, which the guidance says not to construct, and no recorded evidence shows the candidate producing it. Even then, verify.mjs:165-170 does not fail with an unrelated timeout. It reports &#39;[verify] FAIL phase=render step=0 &lt;slug&gt;: [data-presentation-root] did not appear&#39;, which names both the phase and the step. (1) Every readiness wait has a timeout. verify&#39;s startPreview loops against `deadline = Date.now() + 30_000`, each probe has `req.setTimeout(1000, () =&gt; req.destroy())`, and it throws &#39;not ready ... within 30s&#39; when the deadline passes. inspect&#39;s startPreview checks PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT_MS (30s), stops the preview and throws. (2) The build completes before the preview starts. verify&#39;s main() does `await runBuild()`, which resolves only on the build child&#39;s exit with code 0, before `await startPreview()`. inspect runs `spawnSync(&#39;npm&#39;, [&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;])` and checks its status before startPreview. (3) Readiness is an HTTP probe, not a parsed ready URL. stdout and stderr are only buffered for error messages, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. The template copies hold identical code at the same line numbers. Judges A and B are borne out. Judge C&#39;s reason, that inspect&#39;s fetch() has no per-request abort signal, does not decide the clause. The readiness wait is still bounded by its deadline loop, and Node&#39;s fetch has built-in connect and header timeouts.
